comment: gpt-oss-20B served from the OFFICIAL openai/gpt-oss-20b checkpoint (native
MXFP4 MoE experts). Calibration (rotations + VQ codebook) was captured by
loading this SAME checkpoint and letting transformers dequantize it to
bf16 for the forward passes (Mxfp4Config(dequantize=True) -- there is no
native MXFP4 compute path for calibration) -- see
pipelines/oscar_e2e/gptoss_calibrate.py:108-124 and
logs/build_gptoss_mxfp4*.log ('MXFP4 checkpoint -> dequantizing to bf16').
This is the checkpoint-consistent pairing: compare against
gptoss20b_bf16_v1.json, which calibrates AND serves the unsloth bf16
upcast instead. The two must never be cross-wired (mxfp4 rotations/
codebook served against the unsloth checkpoint or vice versa) -- that
mismatch is exactly what every prior gpt-oss-mxfp4 cell in this repo did
(healthy/vq2mx_* served unsloth/gpt-oss-20b-BF16; niah8k_postmerge served
the real checkpoint but with the OLDER unsloth-calibrated bundle, since
it predates this calibration build by ~2h). No cell has combined the two
correctly yet -- this protocol is what closes that gap.
vq2 = VQ for K (SGLANG_VQ_CODEBOOK_PATH, group-VQ gather kernel) + OSCAR
SST rotation + int2 for V (SGLANG_OSCAR_V_ROTATION_PATH) -- this is what
--vq2 always does in serve_oscar.sh, not a per-protocol choice; K's own
OSCAR rotation/clip env is set but ignored by the VQ encoder.
Three knobs below (moe_runner_backend, quant_group_size=0,
absorb_v_rotation=0) are architecture-mandatory for gpt-oss's hybrid-SWA
layout (12 of 24 layers full-attention; only those get a quant pool), not
protocol choices -- see serve_oscar.sh:160-164 and
notes/page_quant/studies/throughput_benchmark.md 'gpt-oss-20B integration'
for the three boot blockers these work around (MoE routing NameError,
fa3 hybrid-attn crash, absorb-rotation contiguous-layer assumption).
TP=2 and every other serve knob below (max_reqs, kv_splits, cuda_graph_bs,
mem_frac) match the validated recipe in logs/_scratch/boot_vq2_mx.sh and
the report14 SS10.5 shadow-fix study -- not re-derived here.
Task grid: NIAH (4 lengths) + math500 + aime25 + gpqa. All rows are
client-ready exports (a pre-templated 'prompt' field per record) built via
pipelines/eval/export_prompt_rows.py -- gpqa_gptoss.jsonl (198 rows) uses
kvq/benchmarks/gpqa_adapter.py's seeded-permutation + simple-evals
template, empty answer_prefix (channel-tag fix correctly skipped, same as
math500/aime25), default 8192-token budget (no override, matching
qwen3_8b_v1.json's gpqa task -- GPQA answers are short, unlike AIME/
math500 proofs). niah_131072 exists but is EXCLUDED: no cell has ever served
gpt-oss above ctx=98304 (the throughput study's validated ceiling, itself
only for bf16); serving 131072 needs ctx >131072, unvalidated on this
stack. Extend ctx and add the task once that's been smoke-tested.
Seed convention (user decision, 2026-07-28): NIAH uses 3 seeds.
Sampling is temperature=1.0/top_p=1.0/top_k=-1 (disabled), per OpenAI's
own gpt-oss repo: 'We recommend sampling with temperature=1.0 and
top_p=1.0' (github.com/openai/gpt-oss README) -- NOT the Qwen protocol's
T=0.6/top_p=0.95/top_k=20, which is a Qwen-specific convention that
doesn't transfer. This supersedes the earlier greedy/single-sample
choice (every historical gpt-oss NIAH cell in the repo was greedy;
3-seed sampling over 1 is an explicit change, not an oversight). Rows
are the 200-row balanced subsets (25/subtask, round-robin ordered) under
artifacts/prompt_rows_proto/niah_<len>_gptoss_s200.jsonl -- built from
the SAME 800-row channel-tag-fixed exports (niah_<len>_gptoss.jsonl) via
the construction method reverse-engineered from Samuel's
samuel_pull_20260727.zip (verified byte-identical against his Qwen s200
files before reuse here).
vq2 uses the CUDA stage-1 decode kernel (vq2_cuda_geom below), not the
Triton kernel. Verified 2026-07-28: 800-row niah_8192 3-way comparison
(baseline / Triton-optimized / CUDA) showed no accuracy regression on
either optimized path (94.1/93.2/93.4 8-task avg, all deltas noise-level)
and confirmed genuine kernel activation via the server log's
'[vq2_cuda] CUDA stage-1 ACTIVE' line, not a silent Triton fallback.
CAVEAT: the CUDA-kernel geometry generalization for gpt-oss (16,256,64,8
-- Qwen's (32,256,128,4) was the only previously-supported geometry) is
UNCOMMITTED in vendor/OSCAR-vq as of this protocol version -- this
protocol has a hard dependency on engine working-tree state that isn't
captured by the engine.sha in provenance.json. Commit it before treating
any cell run against this protocol as reproducible from a clean clone.
exact_chunked_prefill: false reproduces the published serving default.
This is the SAME open decision as the Qwen protocol, but far more
consequential here -- report14 SS10.4/10.5 measured healthy300 chunk-4096
collapsing 89.00->67.33 (-21.7) without the shadow fix, driven ~3/4 by
VQ-K and ~1/4 by INT2-V. Do not quote a chunked gpt-oss vq2 headline
number without deciding this field first.
quarot arm (added 2026-07-28, user request): serve_oscar.sh --int2plain,
HADAMARD_ORDER=64, no K/V clip (ratio=1.0) -- OSCAR's calibration-free
Table-2 baseline (fixed Hadamard rotation, no rotzoo/codebook needed; the
protocol's rot_dir/vq_codebook fields are simply unused for this arm).
HADAMARD_ORDER=64, NOT the usual 128: the plain-int2 kernel asserts
head_dim % hadamard_order == 0 (fused_hadamard_int2_kv.py), and gpt-oss's
head_dim is 64 (vs Qwen/Llama's 128, where every prior quarot cell in this
repo used order=128) -- order=64 is 'full Hadamard over head_dim' for
THIS model, the correct QuaRot definition, not a downgrade. Caught by the
niah_smoke gate: order=128 crashed instantly with 'head_dim (64) must be
divisible by hadamard_order (128)' on the very first decode step.
CAVEAT, unresolved as of this protocol version: --int2plain is a
completely separate serving path from the mixed-KV pool the other three
arms share (SGLANG_ENABLE_MIXED_KV_WINDOWS is never set), and critically
it NEVER sets SGLANG_OSCAR_ABSORB_V_ROTATION -- the gpt-oss hybrid-SWA fix
(ABSORB_V_ROT=0) that every other arm on this protocol depends on. Every
prior quarot/int2plain run in this repo is Llama-3.1-8B or Qwen3-8B
(dense models); this is the first time it has ever been pointed at
gpt-oss's hybrid full-attention/sliding-window layer mix. Smoke-test on
niah_smoke before trusting any quarot cell -- near-zero NIAH retrieval
would signal the plain pool mishandles gpt-oss's SWA layers, not just a
boot crash.
Sync note: this protocol's rotations/codebook are manifest group
'gptoss_mxfp4', but the NIAH row files (both the s200 subsets and the
800-row full exports) live under manifest group 'gptoss' (shared with
gptoss20b_bf16_v1.json). Sync BOTH groups.
